claims.text: A thin, conformal ceria-based overlayer will improve the low-temperature oxidation activity of the near-equiatomic multi-principal-element automotive alloy catalyst.
The ceria-based overlayer will increase resistance to poisoning by H2O and NO.
The ceria-based overlayer will improve catalyst lifetime durability.
Applying the ceria-based overlayer will not increase platinum-group-metal use.
The initial catalyst is a near-equiatomic multi-principal-element alloy containing minimal platinum-group metals.
The unmodified catalyst has adequate catalytic activity under clean conditions.
The unmodified catalyst rapidly loses performance upon exposure to typical automotive exhaust poisons.
The unmodified catalyst loses performance during long-term thermal aging.
A conformal ceria-based overlayer maintains a high dispersion of active sites by reducing sintering.
The ceria-based overlayer provides oxygen-storage and redox capability at the catalyst surface.
The ceria-based coating facilitates rapid oxygen exchange at low temperatures through oxygen storage and release.
The ceria-based coating protects active sites from poisoning by H2O and NO.
The ceria-based coating hinders nanoparticle agglomeration during high-temperature excursions.
Faster oxygen exchange enhances oxidation of CO and hydrocarbons.
Poison protection and suppression of agglomeration preserve catalytic activity during long-term operation.
Relative to the unmodified catalyst, the coated catalyst will retain more catalytic activity after extended high-temperature aging cycles.
The predicted improvements apply at approximately 100–150 °C in exhaust containing CO, hydrocarbons, H2O, and NO.
Periodic excursions to approximately 700 °C can mimic mileage-related thermal degradation over a vehicle lifetime.
The redox and sintering-inhibition effects of ceria-based coatings are well established.
